I audited which of the six hook files are actually wired, expecting to find several dead. **Mostly good news, and one real gap.**

`settings.json` arms exactly one file — `ledger.mjs`. My first reading was that the three guards were dead. They are not: `ledger.mjs` dynamic-imports all three on every write, and all three load cleanly. I checked before saying anything, having nearly made this exact mistake once already today.

## What is actually wrong

**1. `prompt-relay.mjs` is armed to nothing.** It needs a `UserPromptSubmit` entry and there are zero of those in settings. Confirmed, not assumed. This is why I wake on a timer instead of when you speak — the one measurably fixable stage of the 29-minute delay.

**2. A guard that throws looks exactly like a guard that passed.** All three are wrapped in `try { … } catch {}` with nothing logged. A worker today reasoned "syntax-guard blocked nothing, so my file is probably fine" — an absence a silent catch produces just as readily as a real pass.

**3. `syntax-guard` could never have caught this morning's break.** It checks a file *parses*. `a.attr("href", url)` parses perfectly and fails at runtime. The guard worked correctly; the mistake was simply outside it. Which is exactly why the page watcher matters, and why its blind spot — fixed today, still needs the restart — was the expensive half.

Nothing here needs you except the `UserPromptSubmit` line, which is already on your list.
